objective: Calculate the 2010-12-31 -> 2019-12-31 compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of home values for 8 house types in each US state, quantify the within-state growth-rate disparity (max - min CAGR across the 8 house types), and output the top 5 states by disparity to top5_cagr_disparity.csv.

observed_structure.date_columns: 291 monthly ZHVI columns in 'YYYY-MM-DD' headers, 1996-01-31 .. 2020-03-31, float64
observed_structure.region_level: All rows are RegionType == 'State' (50 states + District of Columbia)

steps.name: Data loading and column identification
actions: Read header only to confirm the presence and position of the '2010-12-31' and '2019-12-31' date columns (no full-file scan of irrelevant columns needed since rows are only 51).
Read each file selecting only RegionName, RegionType, StateName, '2010-12-31', '2019-12-31'.
Assign property type from the file name per the mapping table.
Validation: assert 51 rows, RegionType == 'State' only, no duplicated RegionName, no NaN/zero/negative values on the two target dates, identical region sets across files.
steps.output: in-memory long table: region_name, state_name, property_type, v2010, v2019

steps.name: CAGR calculation
actions: cagr = (v2019 / v2010)^(1/9) - 1, with 9 = number of year intervals between 2010-12-31 and 2019-12-31.
Guard: only compute where v2010 > 0 and v2019 > 0; report count of skipped rows (expected 0).
Merged result frame with exactly 3 analysis columns: region_name, property_type, cagr (plus state_name and raw start/end values kept for auditability).
Validation: 51 regions x 8 property types = 408 rows; cagr range sanity check (should be positive, plausibly 0-15%/yr); cross-check a couple of states numerically.

steps.name: State-level disparity statistics
actions: Group by region_name, take max(cagr), min(cagr), count (must equal 8).
Also record argmax/argmin property types and mean/median CAGR for interpretation.
Sort by growth rate difference descending; select top 5 states.
Tie-breaking: on equal disparity, sort by region_name ascending for determinism.

steps.name: Result output and report
actions: Write top5_cagr_disparity.csv with columns exactly ['region name', 'growth rate difference'] (camel-free, as specified).
Growth rate difference expressed in percentage points rounded to 4 decimals (value kept in decimal CAGR units in the full detail file).
Write an accompanying markdown/JSON report summarizing method, validation results, top-5 ranking, which house types drive the extremes, and limitations.

units.growth rate difference: percentage points (max CAGR - min CAGR, x100), rounded to 4 dp

validation_checks: 8 files x 51 states = 408 (state, type) observations, no duplicates
target date columns exist in every file at the expected positions
no NaN / non-positive values on the two target dates
every state has exactly 8 property types in the disparity step
spot check: USA aggregate CAGR for All homes roughly (643270/89137)-style ~ around 6-7%/yr given min/max in profile
assumptions_and_risks: The 9-year exponent assumes exactly 9 annual intervals between 2010-12-31 and 2019-12-31 (correct: 2011..2019).
Property type is not a column in the source files; it is derived from file names (documented mapping).
'District of Columbia' is included as a region although it is not a state (consistent with Zillow's state-level file).
Comparisons are nominal ZHVI growth, not inflation-adjusted.
Files are small (51 rows) so full in-memory pandas processing is safe; run_python 120s limit is far from binding.
